re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **PR #**: 911
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/911
- **Title**: ci(quality): per-function CRAP ratchet — CRAP may only decrease
- **Author**: IstiN

- **Updated**: 2026-10-15T22:30:08Z

## PR Description

Replaces the max-CRAP threshold (4879.8) with a per-function ratchet.

**Baseline** (`crap-baseline.json`, main @ 4e2b9ea): 5280 functions, max CRAP 4475.3 (`_createAdoProvider`, js/common/scm.js), 551 functions > 8, statement coverage 85.8%.

**Gate** (job `crap` in Quality — the required check; coverage from the unit suite run in the same job):
- fails if any function in the baseline gets a higher CRAP
- fails if a function not in the baseline exceeds 8
- passes with improvements reported in the job summary; re-baseline to lock them in

**Tool**: crap4js forked to IstiN/crap4js and extended with `--baseline` / `--write-baseline` (b7e0fd1, 332/332 tests pass). Upstream v0.15.0 only supported a global max threshold.

**Labels**: `crap:regression` set on failure / removed on pass, `crap:improved` when CRAP drops.

Local proof: unchanged tree → 0 regressions (exit 0, stable across two coverage runs); adding branches to `resolveMachineAuthor` → `REGRESSION js/common/machineAuthor.js::resolveMachineAuthor: 5 -> 11`, exit 2.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. crap-baseline.json records every function's
# CRAP score; the gate fails when
#   - a function in the baseline gets a higher CRAP, or
#   - a function not in the baseline (new/renamed) exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD.
# Improvements pass and are reported; lock them in by re-baselining:
#   crap4js . --coverage <coverage-final.json> --baseline crap-baseline.json --write-baseline
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in this same job (instrumented tree),
# so the ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the PR head.
#
# Labels: the job sets crap:regression on a failing PR and removes it when the
# ratchet passes; crap:improved marks PRs that lowered CRAP.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js
# v0.15.0 + --baseline ratchet). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'b7e0fd1d58563bd52aa333a905e29342ebdfd7e8'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js ratchet (per-function baseline)
        id: ratchet
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline crap-baseline.json | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Label PR (crap:regression / crap:improved)
        if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ steps.ratchet.outcome }}
          IMPROVED: ${{ steps.ratchet.outputs.improved }}
        run: |
          if [ "$OUTCOME" = "failure" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:regression || true
          elif [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --remove-label crap:regression || true
          fi
          if [ "$IMPROVED" = "true" ] && [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:improved || true
          fi

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

Actually, wait — let me think. The note was about local verification. Hmm, does npm create different bin links on different platforms? On Linux, npm creates a symlink in node_modules/.bin pointing to the package's bin script. If the bin script uses `import.meta.url === process.argv[1]` (i.e., `if (import.meta.url === \`file://${process.argv[1]}\`) to detect direct execution, then when invoked THROUGH the symlink, process.argv[1] = path of the resolved script? No — process.argv[1] is the path as invoked (the symlink path, not resolved)... Actually when you exec a symlink to an ESM file... wait, a bin file needs a shebang. blocks.text:
Excellent! Two critical findings:

1. **The fork's pinned commit exists and I can read its source.** Key details from `src/baseline.js`:
   - `EPSILON = 0.05` — the ratchet tolerates float noise up to 0.05. But rounding: `score = round(metric.crapScore)` (rounds to 1 decimal), `before` is also rounded to 1 decimal. A regression triggers when `score > before + 0.05`. Since both are 1-decimal values, a jump from 30.0 → 30.1 = 0.1 > 0.05 → REGRESSION. So coverage jitter of even ~0.2% on a CC=10 function creates a false regression. Hmm — how much coverage delta produces 0.1 CRAP delta? CRAP = CC + CC²(1-cov). dCRAP/dcov = -CC²/100 percent. For CC=10: 1.0 percent. So 0.1 delta = 0.1% coverage jitter on that function. Statement coverage jitter of 0.1% per function is entirely possible between runs (flaky tests, timing, mock gaps). For CC=20, dCRAP = 4.0/percent → 0.1 delta = 0.025% jitter. So epsilon 0.05 is VERY tight — effectively any sub-0.1% coverage variation on a function flags. This validates my flakiness concern as a real design property: **the fork's epsilon (0.05) absorbs only float rounding noise, not run-to-run coverage jitter**. The author's local proof: "stable across two coverage runs" — two runs is a weak stability proof. CI harness has known mock-gap failures (~108) which might vary run to run (the note says warnings). If the harness failure set is deterministic, fine. But e.g. any time-dependent code paths covered/non-covered by timing could jitter. IMPORTANT finding: recommend a larger tolerance (e.g. compare with epsilon ~1.0) or document re-baselining discipline for flakes. But wait — the tool is pinned; the workflow can't change epsilon. The finding becomes: "known risk — coverage jitter > 0.1 CRAP flips functions to regression; consider forking epsilon or accepting re-baseline churn". Severity: IMPORTANT (operational flakiness risk; may cause false blocks on unrelated PRs).

   - Output format confirmed: `CRAP Ratchet\n============`, lines `REGRESSION key: before -> score`, `NEW > 8 key: score`, `improved key: before -> score`, and a summary line. So:
     - `sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p'` — matches the `CRAP Ratchet` header. ✔
     - `grep -q '^improved '` — matches `improved ` lines. ✔ Both grep patterns are correct.
   
   - **Error message goes to stderr**: `ctx.err.write('CRAP ratchet failed: CRAP may only decrease.\n')` — with `| tee crap.txt`, stderr bypasses tee → the "CRAP ratchet failed" line is NOT in crap.txt and NOT in the step summary. Minor: the step summary shows the ratchet block (regressions listed in the block itself), so acceptable. But REGRESSION lines go to stdout (formatComparison → ctx.out.write) → tee'd → sed'd into summary. ✔ OK.

   - Exit code 2 on failure, 0 pass, 1 on baseline read error. The workflow propagates `code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}`. ✔

   - **`--write-baseline` writes to `path.resolve(ctx.cwd, opts.baseline)`** — note in the re-baseline flow. Fine.

   - **baselineVerdict: `if (opts.writeBaseline) { ... return 0; }` — write-baseline ALWAYS passes (exit 0), even if regressions exist.** That's the documented flow.

   - **NEW > threshold uses `opts.thresholdValue`** — `--threshold 8`. In ratchet mode, the threshold ALSO still applies globally? Look at runWithOpts: `if (opts.baseline) return baselineVerdict(...)` — replaces reportVerdict entirely. So in ratchet mode the ONLY threshold application is newOverThreshold for functions absent from baseline. Known functions never fail the global threshold — only growth. ✔ Matches the documented policy.

   - Key disambiguation: same-named functions in a file get `#n` by SOURCE ORDER — "the key survives line shifts but not reordering of same-named functions (acceptable — those are rare and fail safe as 'new')". Wait — reordering same-named functions changes which one gets #2 → the baseline values apply to swapped functions → possible false regression/improvement. "Fail safe as new" only if the count changes. If two same-named functions SWAP positions, keys #2/#3 map to different code → one may show a fake regression, the other a fake improvement. Edge case, acknowledged in fork comments. Not this PR's problem (tool design), skip or mention in passing.

   - **Removed functions**: `removed` computed and reported in the summary count, but NOT a failure. Stale baseline entries accumulate (removed functions stay in baseline.functions forever until a re-baseline). The summary line reports `${removed.length} removed` — so visibility exists; re-baseline cleans. OK — suggestion-level at most (baseline hygiene: re-baseline when removed count grows). Actually the workflow header says re-baseline to lock improvements — also cleans removals. Fine, skip or fold into a suggestion.

2. **Labels**: `gh label list` — the 50-label output shows NO `crap:regression` or `crap:improved` labels in the repo! The list was limited to 50 and returned 30 entries, so this is the complete list: bug, documentation, duplicate, enhancement, good first issue, help wanted, invalid, question, wontfix, chore:pin, ai_validating, validation_failed, ai_validated, agent:dev, status:In Development, status:Ready For Development, agent:review, needs-human, ai_pr_reviewed, agent:rework, agent:skip, status:In Review, ai_developed, status:In Rework, sm_story_rework_triggered, rework-round-1, pr_approved, rework-round-2, blocked, status:Done. That's 30 < 50, so complete. **`crap:regression` and `crap:improved` do NOT exist in the repo.**

   Consequence: `gh pr edit --add-label crap:regression` fails with "could not add label: 'crap:regression' not found" → `|| true` swallows it → the labeling feature silently does nothing. The PR description explicitly claims "Labels: crap:regression set on failure / removed on pass, crap:improved when CRAP drops" — this claim is currently FALSE for this repo; the workflow will never set any label. This is a real BLOCKING-ish finding? Let's think about severity: the gate itself (exit code) works — the required check still fails PRs. The label feature is auxiliary (machine SM consumes labels? Let me check if anything consumes crap:regression label... grep in repo: sm.json rules? Let me grep for "crap:" in sm.json and js/. Earlier grep across *.yml/*.md/*.json found only quality.yml. So no automation consumes the label — it's informational for humans. Given the feature silently no-ops and is advertised in the workflow header + PR description, this is at least IMPORTANT. Is it BLOCKING? The label functionality is part of the PR's stated feature set; shipping it broken (silently) = the PR doesn't deliver what it claims. Hmm. The verdict rules: BLOCKING = "correctness/bug findings: broken behavior...". A feature that never works = broken behavior. But it doesn't break existing behavior (labels are new). I'd classify as IMPORTANT leaning BLOCKING... Let me be careful.

   The fix is trivial: `gh label create crap:regression` once (repo-level config, not code). It's a one-time repo setup step the author forgot. The workflow code itself is fine. Machine-protocol: BLOCKING = merge would cause a bug/broken gate. The gate works; the label side-feature silently no-ops → its failure mode is "no label appears" — no data loss, no CI break. The actual verdict block lines (`CRAP Ratchet`, `============`, `0 regression(s), 0 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), X removed`) should appear in stdout after the CRAP Report table. Hold on — maybe the log output got truncated in my grep due to the broken pipe (grep: write error: Broken pipe in first command — because I piped to head). Replaces the max-CRAP threshold (4879.8) with a per-function ratchet.

**Labels**: `crap:regression` set on failure / removed on pass, `crap:improved` when CRAP drops.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. crap-baseline.json records every function's
# CRAP score; the gate fails when
#   - a function in the baseline gets a higher CRAP, or
#   - a function not in the baseline (new/renamed) exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD.
# Improvements pass and are reported; lock them in by re-baselining:
#   crap4js . --coverage <coverage-final.json> --baseline crap-baseline.json --write-baseline
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in this same job (instrumented tree),
# so the ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the PR head.
#
# Labels: the job sets crap:regression on a failing PR and removes it when the
# ratchet passes; crap:improved marks PRs that lowered CRAP.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js
# v0.15.0 + --baseline ratchet). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'b7e0fd1d58563bd52aa333a905e29342ebdfd7e8'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js ratchet (per-function baseline)
        id: ratchet
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline crap-baseline.json | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Label PR (crap:regression / crap:improved)
        if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ steps.ratchet.outcome }}
          IMPROVED: ${{ steps.ratchet.outputs.improved }}
        run: |
          if [ "$OUTCOME" = "failure" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:regression || true
          elif [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --remove-label crap:regression || true
          fi
          if [ "$IMPROVED" = "true" ] && [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:improved || true
          fi

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

So coverage jitter of even ~0.2% on a CC=10 function creates a false regression. Hmm — how much coverage delta produces 0.1 CRAP delta? CRAP = CC + CC²(1-cov). dCRAP/dcov = -CC²/100 percent. For CC=10: 1.0 percent. So 0.1 delta = 0.1% coverage jitter on that function. Statement coverage jitter of 0.1% per function is entirely possible between runs (flaky tests, timing, mock gaps). For CC=20, dCRAP = 4.0/percent → 0.1 delta = 0.025% jitter. So epsilon 0.05 is VERY tight — effectively any sub-0.1% coverage variation on a function flags. This validates my flakiness concern as a real design property: **the fork's epsilon (0.05) absorbs only float rounding noise, not run-to-run coverage jitter**. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

## PR Description

Replaces the max-CRAP threshold (4879.8) with a per-function ratchet.

**Baseline** (`crap-baseline.json`, main @ 4e2b9ea): 5280 functions, max CRAP 4475.3 (`_createAdoProvider`, js/common/scm.js), 551 functions > 8, statement coverage 85.8%.

**Gate** (job `crap` in Quality — the required check; coverage from the unit suite run in the same job):
- fails if any function in the baseline gets a higher CRAP
- fails if a function not in the baseline exceeds 8
- passes with improvements reported in the job summary; re-baseline to lock them in

**Tool**: crap4js forked to IstiN/crap4js and extended with `--baseline` / `--write-baseline` (b7e0fd1, 332/332 tests pass). Upstream v0.15.0 only supported a global max threshold.

**Labels**: `crap:regression` set on failure / removed on pass, `crap:improved` when CRAP drops.

Local proof: unchanged tree → 0 regressions (exit 0, stable across two coverage runs); adding branches to `resolveMachineAuthor` → `REGRESSION js/common/machineAuthor.js::resolveMachineAuthor: 5 -> 11`, exit 2.

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. crap-baseline.json records every function's
# CRAP score; the gate fails when
#   - a function in the baseline gets a higher CRAP, or
#   - a function not in the baseline (new/renamed) exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD.
# Improvements pass and are reported; lock them in by re-baselining:
#   crap4js . --coverage <coverage-final.json> --baseline crap-baseline.json --write-baseline
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in this same job (instrumented tree),
# so the ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the PR head.
#
# Labels: the job sets crap:regression on a failing PR and removes it when the
# ratchet passes; crap:improved marks PRs that lowered CRAP.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js
# v0.15.0 + --baseline ratchet). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'b7e0fd1d58563bd52aa333a905e29342ebdfd7e8'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js ratchet (per-function baseline)
        id: ratchet
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline crap-baseline.json | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Label PR (crap:regression / crap:improved)
        if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ steps.ratchet.outcome }}
          IMPROVED: ${{ steps.ratchet.outputs.improved }}
        run: |
          if [ "$OUTCOME" = "failure" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:regression || true
          elif [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --remove-label crap:regression || true
          fi
          if [ "$IMPROVED" = "true" ] && [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:improved || true
          fi

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

blocks.text:
Excellent! Two critical findings:

1. **The fork's pinned commit exists and I can read its source.** Key details from `src/baseline.js`:
   - `EPSILON = 0.05` — the ratchet tolerates float noise up to 0.05. But rounding: `score = round(metric.crapScore)` (rounds to 1 decimal), `before` is also rounded to 1 decimal. A regression triggers when `score > before + 0.05`. Since both are 1-decimal values, a jump from 30.0 → 30.1 = 0.1 > 0.05 → REGRESSION. So coverage jitter of even ~0.2% on a CC=10 function creates a false regression. Hmm — how much coverage delta produces 0.1 CRAP delta? CRAP = CC + CC²(1-cov). dCRAP/dcov = -CC²/100 percent. For CC=10: 1.0 percent. So 0.1 delta = 0.1% coverage jitter on that function. Statement coverage jitter of 0.1% per function is entirely possible between runs (flaky tests, timing, mock gaps). For CC=20, dCRAP = 4.0/percent → 0.1 delta = 0.025% jitter. So epsilon 0.05 is VERY tight — effectively any sub-0.1% coverage variation on a function flags. This validates my flakiness concern as a real design property: **the fork's epsilon (0.05) absorbs only float rounding noise, not run-to-run coverage jitter**. The author's local proof: "stable across two coverage runs" — two runs is a weak stability proof. CI harness has known mock-gap failures (~108) which might vary run to run (the note says warnings). If the harness failure set is deterministic, fine. But e.g. any time-dependent code paths covered/non-covered by timing could jitter. IMPORTANT finding: recommend a larger tolerance (e.g. compare with epsilon ~1.0) or document re-baselining discipline for flakes. But wait — the tool is pinned; the workflow can't change epsilon. The finding becomes: "known risk — coverage jitter > 0.1 CRAP flips functions to regression; consider forking epsilon or accepting re-baseline churn". Severity: IMPORTANT (operational flakiness risk; may cause false blocks on unrelated PRs).

   - Output format confirmed: `CRAP Ratchet\n============`, lines `REGRESSION key: before -> score`, `NEW > 8 key: score`, `improved key: before -> score`, and a summary line. So:
     - `sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p'` — matches the `CRAP Ratchet` header. ✔
     - `grep -q '^improved '` — matches `improved ` lines. ✔ Both grep patterns are correct.
   
   - **Error message goes to stderr**: `ctx.err.write('CRAP ratchet failed: CRAP may only decrease.\n')` — with `| tee crap.txt`, stderr bypasses tee → the "CRAP ratchet failed" line is NOT in crap.txt and NOT in the step summary. Minor: the step summary shows the ratchet block (regressions listed in the block itself), so acceptable. But REGRESSION lines go to stdout (formatComparison → ctx.out.write) → tee'd → sed'd into summary. ✔ OK.

   - Exit code 2 on failure, 0 pass, 1 on baseline read error. The workflow propagates `code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}`. ✔

   - **`--write-baseline` writes to `path.resolve(ctx.cwd, opts.baseline)`** — note in the re-baseline flow. Fine.

   - **baselineVerdict: `if (opts.writeBaseline) { ... return 0; }` — write-baseline ALWAYS passes (exit 0), even if regressions exist.** That's the documented flow.

   - **NEW > threshold uses `opts.thresholdValue`** — `--threshold 8`. In ratchet mode, the threshold ALSO still applies globally? Look at runWithOpts: `if (opts.baseline) return baselineVerdict(...)` — replaces reportVerdict entirely. So in ratchet mode the ONLY threshold application is newOverThreshold for functions absent from baseline. Known functions never fail the global threshold — only growth. ✔ Matches the documented policy.

   - Key disambiguation: same-named functions in a file get `#n` by SOURCE ORDER — "the key survives line shifts but not reordering of same-named functions (acceptable — those are rare and fail safe as 'new')". Wait — reordering same-named functions changes which one gets #2 → the baseline values apply to swapped functions → possible false regression/improvement. "Fail safe as new" only if the count changes. If two same-named functions SWAP positions, keys #2/#3 map to different code → one may show a fake regression, the other a fake improvement. Edge case, acknowledged in fork comments. Not this PR's problem (tool design), skip or mention in passing.

   - **Removed functions**: `removed` computed and reported in the summary count, but NOT a failure. Stale baseline entries accumulate (removed functions stay in baseline.functions forever until a re-baseline). The summary line reports `${removed.length} removed` — so visibility exists; re-baseline cleans. OK — suggestion-level at most (baseline hygiene: re-baseline when removed count grows). Actually the workflow header says re-baseline to lock improvements — also cleans removals. Fine, skip or fold into a suggestion.

2. **Labels**: `gh label list` — the 50-label output shows NO `crap:regression` or `crap:improved` labels in the repo! The list was limited to 50 and returned 30 entries, so this is the complete list: bug, documentation, duplicate, enhancement, good first issue, help wanted, invalid, question, wontfix, chore:pin, ai_validating, validation_failed, ai_validated, agent:dev, status:In Development, status:Ready For Development, agent:review, needs-human, ai_pr_reviewed, agent:rework, agent:skip, status:In Review, ai_developed, status:In Rework, sm_story_rework_triggered, rework-round-1, pr_approved, rework-round-2, blocked, status:Done. That's 30 < 50, so complete. **`crap:regression` and `crap:improved` do NOT exist in the repo.**

The PR description explicitly claims "Labels: crap:regression set on failure / removed on pass, crap:improved when CRAP drops" — this claim is currently FALSE for this repo; the workflow will never set any label. Let me check if anything consumes crap:regression label... grep in repo: sm.json rules? Let me grep for "crap:" in sm.json and js/. Earlier grep across *.yml/*.md/*.json found only quality.yml. So no automation consumes the label — it's informational for humans. Given the feature silently no-ops and is advertised in the workflow header + PR description, this is at least IMPORTANT. Is it BLOCKING? The label functionality is part of the PR's stated feature set; shipping it broken (silently) = the PR doesn't deliver what it claims. Hmm. The verdict rules: BLOCKING = "correctness/bug findings: broken behavior...". A feature that never works = broken behavior. But it doesn't break existing behavior (labels are new). I'd classify as IMPORTANT leaning BLOCKING... Let me be careful.

Machine-protocol: BLOCKING = merge would cause a bug/broken gate. The gate works; the label side-feature silently no-ops → its failure mode is "no label appears" — no data loss, no CI break. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Replaces the max-CRAP threshold (4879.8) with a per-function ratchet.

**Baseline** (`crap-baseline.json`, main @ 4e2b9ea): 5280 functions, max CRAP 4475.3 (`_createAdoProvider`, js/common/scm.js), 551 functions > 8, statement coverage 85.8%.

- fails if a function not in the baseline exceeds 8
- passes with improvements reported in the job summary; re-baseline to lock them in

**Tool**: crap4js forked to IstiN/crap4js and extended with `--baseline` / `--write-baseline` (b7e0fd1, 332/332 tests pass). Upstream v0.15.0 only supported a global max threshold.

**Labels**: `crap:regression` set on failure / removed on pass, `crap:improved` when CRAP drops.

Local proof: unchanged tree → 0 regressions (exit 0, stable across two coverage runs); adding branches to `resolveMachineAuthor` → `REGRESSION js/common/machineAuthor.js::resolveMachineAuthor: 5 -> 11`, exit 2.
