# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. crap-baseline.json records every function's
# CRAP score; the gate fails when
#   - a function in the baseline gets a higher CRAP, or
#   - a function not in the baseline (new/renamed) exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD.
# Improvements pass and are reported; lock them in by re-baselining:
#   crap4js . --coverage <coverage-final.json> --baseline crap-baseline.json --write-baseline
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in this same job (instrumented tree),
# so the ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the PR head.
#
# Labels: the job sets crap:regression on a failing PR and removes it when the
# ratchet passes; crap:improved marks PRs that lowered CRAP.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js
# v0.15.0 + --baseline ratchet). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'b7e0fd1d58563bd52aa333a905e29342ebdfd7e8'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js ratchet (per-function baseline)
        id: ratchet
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline crap-baseline.json | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Label PR (crap:regression / crap:improved)
        if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ steps.ratchet.outcome }}
          IMPROVED: ${{ steps.ratchet.outputs.improved }}
        run: |
          if [ "$OUTCOME" = "failure" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:regression || true
          elif [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --remove-label crap:regression || true
          fi
          if [ "$IMPROVED" = "true" ] && [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:improved || true
          fi

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

1. **The fork's pinned commit exists and I can read its source.** Key details from `src/baseline.js`:
   - `EPSILON = 0.05` — the ratchet tolerates float noise up to 0.05. But rounding: `score = round(metric.crapScore)` (rounds to 1 decimal), `before` is also rounded to 1 decimal. A regression triggers when `score > before + 0.05`. Since both are 1-decimal values, a jump from 30.0 → 30.1 = 0.1 > 0.05 → REGRESSION. So coverage jitter of even ~0.2% on a CC=10 function creates a false regression. Hmm — how much coverage delta produces 0.1 CRAP delta? CRAP = CC + CC²(1-cov). dCRAP/dcov = -CC²/100 percent. For CC=10: 1.0 percent. So 0.1 delta = 0.1% coverage jitter on that function. Statement coverage jitter of 0.1% per function is entirely possible between runs (flaky tests, timing, mock gaps). For CC=20, dCRAP = 4.0/percent → 0.1 delta = 0.025% jitter. So epsilon 0.05 is VERY tight — effectively any sub-0.1% coverage variation on a function flags. This validates my flakiness concern as a real design property: **the fork's epsilon (0.05) absorbs only float rounding noise, not run-to-run coverage jitter**. The author's local proof: "stable across two coverage runs" — two runs is a weak stability proof. CI harness has known mock-gap failures (~108) which might vary run to run (the note says warnings). If the harness failure set is deterministic, fine. But e.g. any time-dependent code paths covered/non-covered by timing could jitter. Minor: the step summary shows the ratchet block (regressions listed in the block itself), so acceptable. So in ratchet mode the ONLY threshold application is newOverThreshold for functions absent from baseline. Known functions never fail the global threshold — only growth. ✔ Matches the documented policy.

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: Ratchet verdict never reaches the CI log/step summary — `process.exit()` truncates piped stdout**

The fork's entrypoint is `process.exit(main(...))` (`IstiN/crap4js` @ `b7e0fd1`, `src/cli.js:376`), and `runWithOpts` writes the full CRAP Report table (~5280 functions, several hundred KB) **before** the `CRAP Ratchet` verdict block (`formatComparison`). When stdout is a pipe — exactly what `| tee` creates here — only the first ~64 KB (kernel pipe buffer) is flushed before `process.exit()` discards the rest.

**Evidence from this PR's own CI run** ([Quality run 38817446784](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/38817446784/job/116705572771)):
- The ratchet step's stdout ends mid-line at a bare `m` (truncated table row) — no `CRAP Ratchet` block, no `0 regression(s)...` line.
- `IMPROVED` was empty and `sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p'` appended nothing → the step summary is empty.
- Reproduced minimally: a process writing 3000 rows + a verdict block then `process.exit(0)` piped to `tee` delivers only 683 rows (≈64 KB); redirected to a file it delivers all 3004. It worked in your local proof because TTY stdout is synchronous.

**Consequences in CI:**
1. "Passes with improvements reported in the job summary" (workflow header + PR description) never happens — `sed` matches nothing.
2. `crap:improved` can never be set: `grep -q '^improved '` scans a file that provably never contains the verdict block.
3. On a **red** run the exit code still fails the required check, but the log shows only the stderr one-liner `CRAP ratchet failed: CRAP may only decrease.` — not *which* function regressed (`REGRESSION js/...: 5 -> 11` lines are in the dropped tail). Every regression round starts blind.

**Fix (workflow-only, verified):** redirect to a file instead of piping — Node writes to regular files synchronously on POSIX, so nothing is lost:

```yaml
run: |
  set +e
  "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
    --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
    --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
    --baseline crap-baseline.json > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
  code=$?
  cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
  sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
  exit $code
```

Optionally also fix the fork properly (`process.exitCode = code` instead of `process.exit(code)`, or await stdout drain) and bump the pin — that fixes it for every consumer of the tool.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: Static CRAP badges are guaranteed to go stale**

The three shields (`CRAP max-4475.3`, `CRAP > 8-551 fns`, `coverage-85.8%`) are hardcoded snapshots of the baseline at merge time, but this workflow's explicit policy is that these numbers *decrease* and are re-baselined to lock improvements in. After the first re-baseline PR the README will understate the repo's quality (e.g. still showing max 4475.3 after it drops), with no automation to refresh them.

Options:
- Keep only the dynamic `Quality` workflow badge and drop the static numbers, or
- Link the numbers to the baseline file (e.g. a tiny CI step that rewrites the shields into a generated `docs/quality.json` consumed via a dynamic badge service), or
- At minimum, mark them as "snapshot @ ratchet baseline v1" so readers know they drift.

Cosmetic — doesn't block merge.
"}

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. crap-baseline.json records every function's
# CRAP score; the gate fails when
#   - a function in the baseline gets a higher CRAP, or
#   - a function not in the baseline (new/renamed) exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD.
# Improvements pass and are reported; lock them in by re-baselining:
#   crap4js . --coverage <coverage-final.json> --baseline crap-baseline.json --write-baseline
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in this same job (instrumented tree),
# so the ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the PR head.
#
# Labels: the job sets crap:regression on a failing PR and removes it when the
# ratchet passes; crap:improved marks PRs that lowered CRAP.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js
# v0.15.0 + --baseline ratchet). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'b7e0fd1d58563bd52aa333a905e29342ebdfd7e8'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js ratchet (per-function baseline)
        id: ratchet
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline crap-baseline.json | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Label PR (crap:regression / crap:improved)
        if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ steps.ratchet.outcome }}
          IMPROVED: ${{ steps.ratchet.outputs.improved }}
        run: |
          if [ "$OUTCOME" = "failure" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:regression || true
          elif [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --remove-label crap:regression || true
          fi
          if [ "$IMPROVED" = "true" ] && [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:improved || true
          fi

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

1. **The fork's pinned commit exists and I can read its source.** Key details from `src/baseline.js`:
   - `EPSILON = 0.05` — the ratchet tolerates float noise up to 0.05. But rounding: `score = round(metric.crapScore)` (rounds to 1 decimal), `before` is also rounded to 1 decimal. A regression triggers when `score > before + 0.05`. Since both are 1-decimal values, a jump from 30.0 → 30.1 = 0.1 > 0.05 → REGRESSION. So coverage jitter of even ~0.2% on a CC=10 function creates a false regression. Hmm — how much coverage delta produces 0.1 CRAP delta? CRAP = CC + CC²(1-cov). dCRAP/dcov = -CC²/100 percent. For CC=10: 1.0 percent. So 0.1 delta = 0.1% coverage jitter on that function. Statement coverage jitter of 0.1% per function is entirely possible between runs (flaky tests, timing, mock gaps). For CC=20, dCRAP = 4.0/percent → 0.1 delta = 0.025% jitter. So epsilon 0.05 is VERY tight — effectively any sub-0.1% coverage variation on a function flags. This validates my flakiness concern as a real design property: **the fork's epsilon (0.05) absorbs only float rounding noise, not run-to-run coverage jitter**. The author's local proof: "stable across two coverage runs" — two runs is a weak stability proof. CI harness has known mock-gap failures (~108) which might vary run to run (the note says warnings). If the harness failure set is deterministic, fine. But e.g. any time-dependent code paths covered/non-covered by timing could jitter. IMPORTANT finding: recommend a larger tolerance (e.g. compare with epsilon ~1.0) or document re-baselining discipline for flakes. But wait — the tool is pinned; the workflow can't change epsilon. The finding becomes: "known risk — coverage jitter > 0.1 CRAP flips functions to regression; consider forking epsilon or accepting re-baseline churn". Minor: the step summary shows the ratchet block (regressions listed in the block itself), so acceptable. Look at runWithOpts: `if (opts.baseline) return baselineVerdict(...)` — replaces reportVerdict entirely. So in ratchet mode the ONLY threshold application is newOverThreshold for functions absent from baseline. Known functions never fail the global threshold — only growth. ✔ Matches the documented policy.

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: Ratchet verdict never reaches the CI log/step summary — `process.exit()` truncates piped stdout**

The fork's entrypoint is `process.exit(main(...))` (`IstiN/crap4js` @ `b7e0fd1`, `src/cli.js:376`), and `runWithOpts` writes the full CRAP Report table (~5280 functions, several hundred KB) **before** the `CRAP Ratchet` verdict block (`formatComparison`). When stdout is a pipe — exactly what `| tee` creates here — only the first ~64 KB (kernel pipe buffer) is flushed before `process.exit()` discards the rest.

**Evidence from this PR's own CI run** ([Quality run 38817446784](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/38817446784/job/116705572771)):
- The ratchet step's stdout ends mid-line at a bare `m` (truncated table row) — no `CRAP Ratchet` block, no `0 regression(s)...` line.
- `IMPROVED` was empty and `sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p'` appended nothing → the step summary is empty.
- Reproduced minimally: a process writing 3000 rows + a verdict block then `process.exit(0)` piped to `tee` delivers only 683 rows (≈64 KB); redirected to a file it delivers all 3004. It worked in your local proof because TTY stdout is synchronous.

**Consequences in CI:**
1. "Passes with improvements reported in the job summary" (workflow header + PR description) never happens — `sed` matches nothing.
2. `crap:improved` can never be set: `grep -q '^improved '` scans a file that provably never contains the verdict block.
3. On a **red** run the exit code still fails the required check, but the log shows only the stderr one-liner `CRAP ratchet failed: CRAP may only decrease.` — not *which* function regressed (`REGRESSION js/...: 5 -> 11` lines are in the dropped tail). Every regression round starts blind.

**Fix (workflow-only, verified):** redirect to a file instead of piping — Node writes to regular files synchronously on POSIX, so nothing is lost:

```yaml
run: |
  set +e
  "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
    --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
    --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
    --baseline crap-baseline.json > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
  code=$?
  cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
  sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
  exit $code
```

Optionally also fix the fork properly (`process.exitCode = code` instead of `process.exit(code)`, or await stdout drain) and bump the pin — that fixes it for every consumer of the tool.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: Static CRAP badges are guaranteed to go stale**

The three shields (`CRAP max-4475.3`, `CRAP > 8-551 fns`, `coverage-85.8%`) are hardcoded snapshots of the baseline at merge time, but this workflow's explicit policy is that these numbers *decrease* and are re-baselined to lock improvements in. After the first re-baseline PR the README will understate the repo's quality (e.g. still showing max 4475.3 after it drops), with no automation to refresh them.

Options:
- Keep only the dynamic `Quality` workflow badge and drop the static numbers, or
- Link the numbers to the baseline file (e.g. a tiny CI step that rewrites the shields into a generated `docs/quality.json` consumed via a dynamic badge service), or
- At minimum, mark them as "snapshot @ ratchet baseline v1" so readers know they drift.

Cosmetic — doesn't block merge.
"}

# pr-911: ci(quality): per-function CRAP ratchet — CRAP may only decrease

## Description

Replaces the max-CRAP threshold (4879.8) with a per-function ratchet.

**Baseline** (`crap-baseline.json`, main @ 4e2b9ea): 5280 functions, max CRAP 4475.3 (`_createAdoProvider`, js/common/scm.js), 551 functions > 8, statement coverage 85.8%.

**Gate** (job `crap` in Quality — the required check; coverage from the unit suite run in the same job):
- fails if any function in the baseline gets a higher CRAP
- fails if a function not in the baseline exceeds 8
- passes with improvements reported in the job summary; re-baseline to lock them in

**Tool**: crap4js forked to IstiN/crap4js and extended with `--baseline` / `--write-baseline` (b7e0fd1, 332/332 tests pass). Upstream v0.15.0 only supported a global max threshold.

**Labels**: `crap:regression` set on failure / removed on pass, `crap:improved` when CRAP drops.

Local proof: unchanged tree → 0 regressions (exit 0, stable across two coverage runs); adding branches to `resolveMachineAuthor` → `REGRESSION js/common/machineAuthor.js::resolveMachineAuthor: 5 -> 11`, exit 2.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. crap-baseline.json records every function's
# CRAP score; the gate fails when
#   - a function in the baseline gets a higher CRAP, or
#   - a function not in the baseline (new/renamed) exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD.
# Improvements pass and are reported; lock them in by re-baselining:
#   crap4js . --coverage <coverage-final.json> --baseline crap-baseline.json --write-baseline
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in this same job (instrumented tree),
# so the ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the PR head.
#
# Labels: the job sets crap:regression on a failing PR and removes it when the
# ratchet passes; crap:improved marks PRs that lowered CRAP.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js
# v0.15.0 + --baseline ratchet). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'b7e0fd1d58563bd52aa333a905e29342ebdfd7e8'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js ratchet (per-function baseline)
        id: ratchet
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline crap-baseline.json | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Label PR (crap:regression / crap:improved)
        if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ steps.ratchet.outcome }}
          IMPROVED: ${{ steps.ratchet.outputs.improved }}
        run: |
          if [ "$OUTCOME" = "failure" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:regression || true
          elif [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --remove-label crap:regression || true
          fi
          if [ "$IMPROVED" = "true" ] && [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:improved || true
          fi

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — CRAP ratchet via crap4js, pinned like crap4dart in dmd.
#
# Threshold policy (owner 2026-09-28): the CRAP bar is NOT lowered to pass —
# the CURRENT measured maximum is fixed as the ratchet baseline, so the code
# can only improve. Baseline: 4879.8 (action/developTicketAndCreatePR.js,
# CC=116 @ 29.3% coverage). Improvements lower the max freely; any change
# that pushes the max ABOVE the baseline fails the gate.
#
# Tool pin: crap4js v0.8.1 by release tag (same discipline as dmd pinning
# crap4dart 0.9.5). Install from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js' package is an
# unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Ratchet baseline — the measured repo-wide maximum CRAP (see header).
  # Re-measure with the steps below; lower it when the code improves.
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '4879.8'
  CRAP4JS_REF: 'v0.8.1'

jobs:
  crap:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

   - `EPSILON = 0.05` — the ratchet tolerates float noise up to 0.05. But rounding: `score = round(metric.crapScore)` (rounds to 1 decimal), `before` is also rounded to 1 decimal. A regression triggers when `score > before + 0.05`. Since both are 1-decimal values, a jump from 30.0 → 30.1 = 0.1 > 0.05 → REGRESSION. So coverage jitter of even ~0.2% on a CC=10 function creates a false regression. Hmm — how much coverage delta produces 0.1 CRAP delta? CRAP = CC + CC²(1-cov). dCRAP/dcov = -CC²/100 percent. For CC=10: 1.0 percent. So 0.1 delta = 0.1% coverage jitter on that function. Statement coverage jitter of 0.1% per function is entirely possible between runs (flaky tests, timing, mock gaps). For CC=20, dCRAP = 4.0/percent → 0.1 delta = 0.025% jitter. So epsilon 0.05 is VERY tight — effectively any sub-0.1% coverage variation on a function flags. This validates my flakiness concern as a real design property: **the fork's epsilon (0.05) absorbs only float rounding noise, not run-to-run coverage jitter**. The author's local proof: "stable across two coverage runs" — two runs is a weak stability proof. CI harness has known mock-gap failures (~108) which might vary run to run (the note says warnings). If the harness failure set is deterministic, fine. But e.g. any time-dependent code paths covered/non-covered by timing could jitter. Interesting! Two revelations:

1. The grep for "regression(s)" in the run log returned NOTHING. That means the `CRAP Ratchet` verdict block was NOT printed in the log?? Wait — the verdict block is written by `formatComparison` → `ctx.out.write` → stdout → tee'd. The sed range `'/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p'` goes to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, not to the log — but tee should ALSO print it to the log (stdout). The log showed the CRAP Report table (from the regular report output), but I didn't see the "CRAP Ratchet" block in the log. My earlier grep `-E "CRAP Ratchet|..."` matched only the sed command echo and... hmm, wait, the first grep output showed only 4 lines before the Label PR section, all command echoes. The actual verdict block lines (`CRAP Ratchet`, `============`, `0 regression(s), 0 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), X removed`) should appear in stdout after the CRAP Report table. My second grep found NOTHING matching "regression\(s\)" — that's suspicious!

Hold on — maybe the log output got truncated in my grep due to the broken pipe (grep: write error: Broken pipe in first command — because I piped to head). The second command had no head... `gh run view --log | grep -E "regression\(s\)|..."` returned nothing. If the block were there, "0 regression(s)" would match. Hmm!

Wait — but `CRAP Ratchet` block IS the expected output. Unless... the fork's `formatComparison` output goes to stdout but the ratchet mode doesn't print the CRAP Report table AND the ratchet block... no wait, the table WAS printed (I saw it). In runWithOpts: analyze → `if (opts.baseline) return baselineVerdict(...)`. Where did the CRAP Report table come from then? Looking at the fork's cli.js diff: runWithOpts analyzes, then `if (opts.baseline) return baselineVerdict(metrics, opts, ctx)`. The table print must be BEFORE that branch — the report is printed as part of analysis (reportVerdict or somewhere). Actually the table could be printed by a separate `ctx.out.write(formatReport(...))` before the verdict functions. So table + ratchet block both on stdout.

But the log grep found no "regression(s)" line! Possibilities:
- The log I fetched is truncated/incomplete (gh run view --log should be complete).

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: Ratchet verdict never reaches the CI log/step summary — `process.exit()` truncates piped stdout**

The fork's entrypoint is `process.exit(main(...))` (`IstiN/crap4js` @ `b7e0fd1`, `src/cli.js:376`), and `runWithOpts` writes the full CRAP Report table (~5280 functions, several hundred KB) **before** the `CRAP Ratchet` verdict block (`formatComparison`). When stdout is a pipe — exactly what `| tee` creates here — only the first ~64 KB (kernel pipe buffer) is flushed before `process.exit()` discards the rest.

**Evidence from this PR's own CI run** ([Quality run 38817446784](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/38817446784/job/116705572771)):
- The ratchet step's stdout ends mid-line at a bare `m` (truncated table row) — no `CRAP Ratchet` block, no `0 regression(s)...` line.
- `IMPROVED` was empty and `sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p'` appended nothing → the step summary is empty.
- Reproduced minimally: a process writing 3000 rows + a verdict block then `process.exit(0)` piped to `tee` delivers only 683 rows (≈64 KB); redirected to a file it delivers all 3004. It worked in your local proof because TTY stdout is synchronous.

**Consequences in CI:**
1. "Passes with improvements reported in the job summary" (workflow header + PR description) never happens — `sed` matches nothing.
2. `crap:improved` can never be set: `grep -q '^improved '` scans a file that provably never contains the verdict block.
3. On a **red** run the exit code still fails the required check, but the log shows only the stderr one-liner `CRAP ratchet failed: CRAP may only decrease.` — not *which* function regressed (`REGRESSION js/...: 5 -> 11` lines are in the dropped tail). Every regression round starts blind.

**Fix (workflow-only, verified):** redirect to a file instead of piping — Node writes to regular files synchronously on POSIX, so nothing is lost:

```yaml
run: |
  set +e
  "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
    --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
    --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
    --baseline crap-baseline.json > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
  code=$?
  cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
  sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
  if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
  exit $code
```

Optionally also fix the fork properly (`process.exitCode = code` instead of `process.exit(code)`, or await stdout drain) and bump the pin — that fixes it for every consumer of the tool.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: Static CRAP badges are guaranteed to go stale**

The three shields (`CRAP max-4475.3`, `CRAP > 8-551 fns`, `coverage-85.8%`) are hardcoded snapshots of the baseline at merge time, but this workflow's explicit policy is that these numbers *decrease* and are re-baselined to lock improvements in. After the first re-baseline PR the README will understate the repo's quality (e.g. still showing max 4475.3 after it drops), with no automation to refresh them.

Options:
- Keep only the dynamic `Quality` workflow badge and drop the static numbers, or
- Link the numbers to the baseline file (e.g. a tiny CI step that rewrites the shields into a generated `docs/quality.json` consumed via a dynamic badge service), or
- At minimum, mark them as "snapshot @ ratchet baseline v1" so readers know they drift.

Cosmetic — doesn't block merge.
